purpose: ONE shared vector for the process-attribution predicate that decides whether a process may be force-killed as ours. Loaded and asserted by BOTH packages/mcp-server/test/test-process-tree.test.js (isOwnedBrowserCommandLine) and packages/extension/src/test/daemon-manager.test.ts (DaemonManager._isOwnedCommandLine criterion b). The predicate has been reimplemented independently on each side (the mcp-server is a standalone npm package and must not depend on the extension); it has drifted apart five times, each drift shipping a force-kill of an innocent process. Editing one implementation and not the other now fails a test on the side that was NOT edited.
rules: expect="owned"     → the command line IS a Chrome-family browser process running EXACTLY our profile, and may be force-killed.
expect="not-owned" → it may NOT be killed, whatever else it is. Both sides must agree.

helper=true        → additionally a Chromium helper (--type=...). ATTRIBUTION is still "owned" on both sides; only the SELECTION policy differs, and that difference is deliberate: packages/mcp-server kills process TREES, so a helper is skipped because its root browser's tree-kill already takes it; the extension kills pids individually and therefore keeps helpers. This is the ONE documented semantic difference between the two call sites.

form="posix"|"win32" → which path spelling the command line is written in; it selects which profile/config path the placeholders expand to. It is NOT a platform gate: both suites run both forms, because canonicalisation (\ → /, lower-case) is what makes the predicate platform-independent.

The `cases` array is the ATTRIBUTION vector — both implementations must return the same verdict for every entry. The other three arrays exist because two of the things worth pinning are not shared: `argvSplits` pins the argv PARSER both sides now depend on, `daemonEntryCases` pins the extension-only bundled-entry criterion (a) (the server has no such criterion, so it must answer not-owned to all of them), and `neighbourEnumeration` is a GENERATOR spec both suites expand into the same cross-product.

AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS PROVES MIRROR PARITY, NOT CORRECTNESS. They are line-for-line ports, so a defect in one is a defect in the other and this vector will faithfully record both agreeing on the wrong answer — that is exactly what happened with the nested-quoted-value defect (`nested-value-*`), which both sides answered "owned" for five rounds. Correctness lives in the `why` of each case being argued on its own merits. Agreement is a regression guard.

placeholders.{PROFILE}: the owned browser profile directory, in this case's path spelling
placeholders.{PROFILE_URL}: the same directory, always forward-slashed (for file:/// URLs)
placeholders.{CFG}: the config directory — the profile's PARENT — used for near-miss cases
placeholders.{ENTRY}: the bundled daemon entry `<ext>/dist/mcp/index.mjs`, in this case's path spelling. Only meaningful in `daemonEntryCases`.

KNOWN IRREDUCIBLE LIMIT, pinned deliberately — this is NOT a shape we want to kill. A FORWARD-SLASH-SPELLED command line — on any host, since the gate is the path spelling and not the platform — that hands another program a CORRECTLY-NAMED macOS bundle executable path is byte-for-byte identical to a real bundle invocation (`/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome`), so no rule over the string can separate them; only the filesystem could. It is pinned as `owned` so that BOTH implementations keep agreeing about it and neither can widen or narrow the limit unnoticed. If a future change makes this `not-owned` WITHOUT losing the real bundle cases (`posix-mac-bundle-*`), that is an improvement — change this case then, deliberately. Mitigation today: it still requires the caller to pass our exact `--user-data-dir=<profile>`, which no ordinary vim/git/tar invocation carries.

daemonEntryCases.purpose: The EXTENSION-ONLY half of ownership: `<extensionPath>/dist/mcp/index.mjs` as a whole argv entry IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWED by the separate entries `daemon` and `start` — the shape `_spawnDetached()` and `daemon/launcher.js` emit. `packages/extension` asserts `expect` against `DaemonManager._isOwnedCommandLine` with `extensionPath = paths[form].ext`. `packages/mcp-server` has NO such criterion, so it asserts that `isOwnedBrowserCommandLine` answers not-owned to EVERY one of these — which is what pins the deliberate site difference instead of leaving it to a comment.

neighbourEnumeration.purpose: A committed, deterministic generator both suites expand into the same cross-product and assert independently. It exists because this predicate has produced eight holes across five rounds and every round fixed the REPORTED spelling and missed its neighbour: enumerating the space mechanically is the only way to stop choosing which neighbours to think of. Every `valueFlags` entry is a real Chrome switch that takes a caller-supplied VALUE, so every one of them can carry our profile flag as text. Expansion is specified in `expansion` below.
expansion: NOT-OWNED: `<image> <flag>=<wrap(style, "--user-data-dir=<PROFILE>")>` for every form x valueFlags x quoteStyles.
OWNED: `<image> --user-data-dir=<wrap(style, "<PROFILE>")>` and `<image> <wrap(style, "--user-data-dir=<PROFILE>")>` for every form x quoteStyles.
wrap("bare", v) = v ; wrap("double", v) = "\"" + v + "\"" ; wrap("single", v) = "'" + v + "'".
